prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
for the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I have moved from zeolite and molecular-sieve design (B033) to a two-part prize: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) and base editing (Liu). The first-round exchange showed me that B033 has no support beyond myself, and Somfai and Sparr both asked for a discovery-level definition that I cannot supply honestly, because zeolite design is a programme with many framework syntheses and several equally strong contributors. I do not move merely to be in a larger group; I move because the two parts pass the test I apply to my own field, which is whether structure and mechanism were established and whether a new capability followed. For C-N coupling the catalytic cycle and the ligand-structure to reactivity relationship are well characterised, the reaction is used at scale in pharmaceuticals, and the attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist. For base editing a deaminase was chemically brought to a chosen base without a double-strand break, a capability that did not exist before 2016, with independent reproduction in many laboratories and clinical use. The two parts have no scientific link and I will not pretend otherwise; each stands on its own citation.
statement.case_against: C-N coupling sits close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and the Kosugi and Migita precedents mean the chronology must be stated carefully in the citation. Base editing is about ten years old, clinical outcomes are still accumulating, and a Liu-only citation leaves out Komor and Gaudelli, whose experiments defined the two editor classes (the adenine editor needed a directed-evolved TadA, which is real enzyme engineering), and sets aside the independent Kondo and Nishida deaminase-fusion work, which as I recall was published after Komor's 2016 cytidine editor but remains a genuine competing claim that our own expert reports must date. A two-part prize without a unifying theme is also somewhat arbitrary. Finally, zeolite design remains in my view the clearest unrecognised case of design of structure for function, and I give it up only because it cannot be written as one discovery with three secure names.

responses.point: Somfai argues that Buchwald and Hartwig are the decisive pair and that Kosugi's stoichiometric tin-amide work is a precursor, not the general method; he also holds that Liu alone is defensible for base editing and that B033 lacks a single decisive discovery.
responses.response: Your criticism of B033 is correct and it is the main reason I have moved: a single verifiable origin, as in Pd amination, is what I could not give for zeolites. I accept Buchwald and Hartwig as the pair, and your line that the general catalytic systems made the reaction routine matches how I read the ligand-structure evidence. I would still ask that the citation state the chronology relative to Kosugi and Migita explicitly, so that the 2010 overlap and the precursor question are answered in the text rather than left to the expert report. On Liu alone I follow you only in part: it is a judgement about leadership, and I would want it said openly that Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida are not dismissed as contributors.

responses.point: Aqvist puts base editing first with Liu alone and Crews and Handa for degradation as a second part, arguing that two distinct achievements keep attribution clean within three names; he doubts that C-N coupling is a completely new capability after 2010.
responses.response: I agree with the two-achievement logic, and with Liu alone only on the condition I set in round 1, that the committee states why the others are excluded. I answer your doubt about B039 directly: ligand-controlled C-N coupling needed different ligands, a different catalytic cycle at the amine-binding and reductive-elimination steps, and a different substrate scope, so I treat it as a distinct principle and not a footnote to Heck, Negishi and Suzuki. That said, B066 is a serious competitor for the second slot. I keep it as an alternative because the Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli and Handa attribution is still split among members and no bifunctional degrader is approved.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first with Liu alone in his file, notes that the trainees Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive experiments, and says Kondo and Nishida's independent work makes a one-person citation hard to defend; he is open to a two-part prize.
responses.response: The Kondo and Nishida question is the honest weak point and I do not think it dissolves by naming trainees. As I recall it, Nishida's Science paper appeared after Komor's Nature paper, and Gaudelli's adenine editor in 2017 had no counterpart in their work; the committee should verify these dates in the expert reports before the vote. Given that, and given that a three-name cap forces a choice, Liu alone is the defensible reading when base editing is one part of two. If the committee settles on base editing as the sole part, I would support Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, because the directed evolution of TadA is real chemistry and then deserves a slot.

responses.point: Brzezinski keeps nitrogenase (Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt) as his first choice and accepts that the cofactor mechanism is open; he sees B066 as the strongest candidate that is not his.
responses.response: We agree on the principle that structural evidence has to carry the claim. I have not moved on nitrogenase for the reason I gave: the structures are secure, but the E4 hydride state and the N2 binding site are not settled, and the citation would overstate what was shown. Your own caution about five credited names applies equally to my former choice, B033. I would reconsider B012 once turnover-state structures resolve the mechanism.

uncertainties: Whether Kondo and Nishida's deaminase-fusion work is dated and scoped such that a Liu-only citation is fair, since my chronology is recalled and not checked.
Whether the committee accepts a two-part prize with no scientific link, or prefers a single-achievement prize, in which case I would move to B062 alone with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli.
Whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize leaves C-N coupling a distinct principle, and how the Kosugi and Migita precedents are placed.
Whether B066 should replace B039 as the second part if the committee can agree on a degradation trio.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1 on the substance. My research field (zeolites, MOFs and porous materials, with electron crystallography of zeolites) is close to B033 and the porous-materials community, but B033 is now an alternative and not in my preferred configuration. I have no known personal, collaborative or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or Liu, and I note that I am a Stockholm University colleague of Peter Brzezinski, which bears on none of the candidates discussed.
